args.text: Cloud-gesture campaign FAILED, rag rescue partially succeeded: filbert-24 gestures at pressure 0.6-0.9 laying storm_dark/storm_mid/glow UNDILUTED on the DRY graded sky came out as opaque flat 'venetian blind' ribbons, far darker/more saturated than the mixed sky below, and crossed the oak canopy. Lesson: a gesture on dry paint is a solid slab of masstone — for clouds the piles must be mixed close to the local sky value, or laid thinner/lower pressure, and clipped away from foreground. Rag rescue (rag 55, dip 0.35, pressure 0.65, 2 passes over y0-345, still open) lifted most ribbon paint down toward dry sky, leaving streaky scud traces that actually read as storm movement in left sky. BUT rag over the oak smeared pale/cream bands and blue crackle traces through lower canopy — canopy must be repainted after drying. Second sky-only rag pass (mask minus canopy grown 12, fresh rag, 0.6, 1 pass) softened remaining dashes. Going forward: clouds to be built with low-contrast graded work passes like the successful lower-sky pass, NOT masstone gestures.
